messages:
maria: Heads-up — got a noisy GPU on cluster-gpua-03. dmesg is spewing repeated NVRM/Xid lines and some ECC warnings. Need a quick checklist for bundling dmesg + journalctl + nvidia-smi for triage.

devon: Ok — first-pass: `dmesg -T --level=err,warn | tail -n 200` and `journalctl -k -b --no-pager | grep -i nvrm` then `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,driver_model,compute_mode --format=csv` to snapshot state.

kai: We should use the logchain agent here to produce a compact bundle and preserve timestamps. Example: `logchain collect --node cluster-gpua-03 --gpus all --since 15m --include nvidia-smi,dmesg,journalctl --out /tmp/gpu-bundle.tgz`

maria: I don't have logchain on that node yet. I'll paste the manual outputs for now.

maria: ```
[  +0.000000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, pid=1723, gpu=0
[  +0.001234] NVRM: Xid 79 indicates a GPU fault.
[  +0.002345] EDAC MC0: ECC error detected on GPU memory
```

ashley: Also grab `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` and `journalctl -u kubelet --since "10m ago"` — we want Pod UIDs and kubelet ops around the reset time. Pod context makes attribution much faster.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-214 assigned to @devon — https://incidents.redwood.local/INC-2026-214

devon: I'll collect nv-host and driver logs. Also run `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name --format=csv,noheader` to see active compute workloads (old nvidia-smi may need different flags).

kai: For longer-term, let's add an extraction rule that normalizes Xid codes into severity buckets (recoverable vs fatal) and extracts the kernel timestamp, PCI address, and driver reset event in a single JSON line. I can PR a parser: `eng-infra/gpu-failure-parser`.

ashley: We should also correlate KV cache hits from the inference runtime — add `kv_cache_hit=` lines from the runtime logs to the bundle if possible. A sudden spike in cache misses before an Xid is an interesting signal.

maria: Timeline I saw: 2026-03-17T14:02:03Z repeated Xid 79s, then driver reset at 14:06:11Z, then pods restart. I'll upload the full tarball to the incident.

devon: Plan: cordon node -> drain non-critical pods -> collect full nv-host and kernel oops -> probe hardware. If device continues to flap after reboot, mark card for replacement.

maria: ACK. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-failure-triage :small_red_triangle: Follow checklist near bottom for forced reimage vs replace.

kai: Follow-ups I will take: (1) add `--since` semantics to logchain for targeted grabs; (2) push the Xid normalization rules; (3) create a tiny upload helper that attaches the bundle to the incident and anonymizes PII.

ashley: +1 on a one-liner for SRE runbook for Xid triage. Something like: `curl -sS https://logchain.redwood/collect | bash -s -- --since 15m --gpus all` — lightweight and documented.

devon: I'm cordoning/draining now, will post status and pv migration notes when done. Ping me in thread if you find new Xid patterns.

maria: Thanks all — uploading artifacts to INC-2026-214 and will link here when available.
